articles.title: Champions League: Silva sparks Real Madrid’s demolition of Leipzig as Lask stun Sporting
articles.summary: Bernardo Silva opens scoring as Madrid win 4-1. Galatasaray sweep past Lille; 10-man Inter edge Shakhtar. Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande among the goals for José Mourinho’s side.
body: Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval.
Mbappé bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on.

“We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible – we’ve won three and there are five to go,” Mbappé said. The France forward, who hopes to win the Ballon d’Or next week, has netted in each of Madrid’s Champions League matches this season and has 12 goals in 12 games.

“I’m doing well [but] I think I can do more,” he said. “I’m one of the few players who always has to demand more from himself... right now it’s a good moment, but we have to keep going and I have to do more.”

articles.title: ‘Angry’ Carrick on the brink as Fernandes hits out at Manchester United tactics
articles.summary: Manager apologises to fans after 4-1 defeat in Como. Captain criticises ‘decision from the staff’ not to press. Michael Carrick’s future as Manchester United manager is in the balance after the club’s humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat away against Como on Wednesday.
body: Before Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford on Sunday his future may be discussed by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the co-owner who controls sporting policy.

On a torrid night, an “angry” Carrick insisted afterwards he had not given his position any thought but was forced to defend himself against his own captain, Bruno Fernandes, who questioned the manager’s tactics of not pressing against Cesc Fàbregas’s team. Carrick in turn criticised his side for not running. The defeat at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia leaves United with only two wins all season from 11 games. They are 13th in the Premier League and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup last month.

Carrick was asked if he fears for his job. “Listen, I’ve not given my own position any thought,” he said. “[My thoughts are] for the supporters – I was one of them watching that and I wasn’t happy at all.”

articles.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
articles.summary: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word.
body: Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged.

Enter Kane. He wore his playmaker’s hat; some of his passing was sumptuous and it was his assist for Alphonso Davies that helped Bayern to draw level. He wore his finisher’s one, too, scoring from the penalty spot to put his team in charge. It meant he had scored in 10 consecutive Champions League games; one short of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record. There is a reason why Kane is the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday. He now has 16 goals against Arsenal; he has only scored more against one club – Leicester, against whom he has 20.

articles.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa maintain perfect start against Viking
articles.summary: For a little over half an hour, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed…
body: Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain.

“Collectively and individually we did a good job and some players also made a step forward in their confidence,” said Emery, who was pleased with Villa’s seriousness against opponents still finding their way in a first campaign at this level. “Each match has an objective to get better, to be consistent and be very demanding.”

The hard work had been done in an opening period whose scoreline hardly did justice to Villa’s total dominance. Viking had drawn at home with Bayern Munich in their previous game, a fact that would look more explicable when they emerged from their shell later, but were barely afforded a kick and looked vulnerable every time the ball was delivered from wide.

articles.summary: Commanders receiver and return man Jaylin Lane had surgery to repair a season-ending ankle injury that he suffered during a Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. He was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 5, after suffering a fracture and dislocation of the ankle.
body: #Commanders WR Jaylin Lane had surgery to repair his fractured and dislocated ankle on Oct. 9, per source. The procedure was successful and he's expected to be cleared for football activities just before OTAs.

Reed also reports that Lane should be ready to return before the Commanders begin OTAs next spring. The injury is a significant one and typically requires an extensive rehab and acclimation to football activities.

Lane is a second-year pro who is already considered among the NFL’s top returners, with two punts returned for a touchdown during his rookie season in 2024. He was also improving as a receiver, so this injury was a real setback to that progress.
The Commanders have been using Luke McCaffrey and at times Rachaad White or Antonio Williams to help with the return duties.

articles.title: Miserable Man Utd ripped apart by Como
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's Manchester United were ripped apart in a dreadful 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League, as their miserable run of results stretched to seven without a win.
body: The pressure continues to pile on Carrick and this United side as their start to the season lurches from bad to worse - and on Wednesday night they were humbled by a Como team that delivered more intensity and quality in Italy.

The first attribute should be a non-negotiable but, despite United's application being in the spotlight, they were once again outworked by their opposition. Static in midfield, allowing Como players to run off them, losing markers... this was a shocking show of United's big failings out of possession.

The tone was set just two minutes in when Man Utd went behind early on - again. They are the first English side to concede in back-to-back Champions League games so soon and never got to grips with Cesc Fabregas' impressively coached team.

Nico Paz brought the class for the hosts. The talented Argentina international stuck the opener into the top corner when Harry Maguire gave him too much space and then slotted in a third after catching Carlos Baleba in possession.

articles.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
articles.summary: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.
body: An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress.
But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.
O'Neill, the newly-crowned Super League Man of Steel, said: "We have discussed what is required but I feel like the mentality can't be any different to what we had against Tonga.

"We can't go into this game thinking about the points difference. We've got to go into this game hard-nosed like we did against Tonga, and hopefully if we do our jobs well enough we're going to get the win."

articles.title: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
articles.summary: Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.
body: Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.
In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.
While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.
